rule: An entry is relevant to a topic if someone asking for everything we have on that topic would want it on the list: the topic is the entry's main subject or a stated core feature. A passing mention, a tag alone, or one item in a long list of unrelated features is not enough. An entry may be relevant to several topics.

topics.definition: Getting text and structure out of documents and images: OCR engines and models, PDF/scan-to-text or -markdown converters, document layout and table parsers, and guides to choosing them.

Running language models on hardware you control: local inference runtimes and servers, quantization and low-VRAM techniques for running models, switching tools between local and cloud models, local setup guides.

Seeing what multiple agents are doing: UIs, dashboards, TUIs, graphs, boards, or trace views that display agents/subagents and their work, including orchestration tools whose visual board is a stated feature.
How agents retain information across turns and sessions: memory layers and servers, memory architectures, benchmarks and surveys of agent memory.
Retrieving information for LLMs or by meaning: RAG pipelines and patterns, vector databases, embedding search, BM25/hybrid ranking, rerankers, ANN index methods.

out.amazon-bedrock: RAG is one feature of many
